claims.statement: Binding Tariff Information is a legal classification decision issued by EU customs authorities, generally valid across the EU for three years and binding on authorities and the holder.
Tariff classification determines customs duty and can also determine non-tariff measures such as licences, restrictions and origin-related requirements.

In Poland, a WIT application and decision are electronic and free; paid value must therefore come from complex fact development, expert review and workflow support rather than access to the official filing itself.

After a complete BTI application is accepted, the authority normally has 120 days to decide, with exceptional extensions possible; a decision based on inaccurate or incomplete applicant information is annulled.
Commercial incumbents already offer AI-assisted or automated tariff classification, bulk processing, APIs, reasoning and human-expert review.
Maersk already offers European HS-classification consulting and customs-clearance support, so a freight forwarder can be both a channel and a direct substitute.

The defensible wedge is more likely a confidential, expert-reviewed evidence and exception workflow for difficult products than a generic code recommender, because official rulings are public and code automation is already crowded.

contrary_evidence: Valid and invalid BTI decisions are already public in the EBTI database, so defensibility must come from confidential fact patterns, workflow distribution and outcome data rather than public rulings.
The official Polish WIT application and decision are free, so the proposed case fee cannot be justified by filing access alone.
Avalara, eClear and TariffPilot already automate classification research and workflow, including APIs, bulk processing and human expertise.
Maersk already sells HS-classification consulting alongside customs clearance, creating channel conflict with a forwarder-embedded product.

economics.acquisition_route: Research update: white-label into smaller freight forwarders and customs agencies at new-SKU intake remains unvalidated. Large forwarders can already provide classification consulting, while software incumbents sell direct, so the initial target should be a forwarder lacking an internal classification stack and willing to pilot non-exclusive expert-reviewed cases.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated scenario, not a forecast: resolve 100 cases in year 1, reach 3 million PLN ARR by year 4, build 3.5 million PLN founder equity and retained cash by year 6, and 5 million PLN founder net worth in years 7-10. No public evidence validates case volume, ARR, retention or valuation assumptions.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated operating estimate: 2-3 hours per day only if qualified customs specialists own opinions, escalations and representation while the founder owns data and workflow automation.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated: 55%-80% after customs-expert review, translation, product-fact development, client follow-up and appeal support; incumbent automation may pressure simple-case prices.
economics.payback: Unvalidated: 8-16 months depends on repeat forwarder case flow and expert cost. The official decision can take 120 days after acceptance, limiting rapid outcome feedback.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 2,000-12,000 PLN per complex case plus 1,000-5,000 PLN monthly forwarder workspace. Because the official Polish WIT application and decision are free, the fee must buy expert-reviewed fact development, audit trail, exception handling or appeal support.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated: repeat follows new SKUs, rule changes and product modifications, but forwarder case frequency, workspace retention and data-reuse permission are not evidenced.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Consented private mappings between product facts, questions, rulings, appeals and landed-cost outcomes improve retrieval and expert efficiency
fingerprint.customer: EU importers and freight forwarders handling novel or ambiguous products
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: White-label insertion into forwarder and customs-agent onboarding of new products
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Structured product evidence, expert review and BTI application support, without pretending to issue a binding ruling
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The importer or forwarder pays for a reviewed case pack and ongoing workflow access
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A new SKU lacks a defensible tariff classification or faces a classification dispute

founder_fit: Strong match for structured evidence retrieval and AI-assisted analysis.
Expert review can be contracted while the founder builds the data system.
The 75,000 PLN initial-capital estimate fits within stated free capital, but part-time feasibility still depends on contracted customs specialists owning opinions and escalations.
risks: Incorrect product facts lead to an invalid or harmful classification.
Public AI tools commoditise simple classification research.
Forwarders may prefer their own consulting and customs-control-tower products rather than embed a third party.
A slow official BTI cycle delays outcome labels and weakens the proposed data flywheel.
Acting as a customs representative without proper empowerment or applicable national conditions creates liability.

structure.commercial_archetype: Expert decision network with case-outcome data cooperative
structure.control_point: Forwarder channel agreements and contractual rights to reuse de-identified product-description, decision and exception outcomes
structure.critical_dependency: Qualified customs expertise, confidentiality-safe data rights, accurate product facts and client acceptance of the BTI process

thesis: Embed with freight forwarders and customs representatives to structure difficult product-classification cases and, with client permission, retain anonymised product-feature, ruling, appeal and realised-cost outcomes. The control point is a private case-outcome network and forwarder distribution, while qualified customs professionals remain responsible for advice and representation.
title: Customs Classification Outcome Cooperative
uncertainties: Scope of activities requiring customs-representative credentials
Value of private outcomes beyond public EBTI records
Willingness to pay 2,000-12,000 PLN when the official Polish WIT process is free
Qualified expert cost and liability allocation per case
Contractual permission to reuse de-identified private fact patterns and realised landed-cost outcomes
